People switching from Windows to Mac have almost no software limitations. Not only do all the largest PC applications run on Mac, but there are countless practical apps that are exclusive to Mac.

The biggest exception is games. However, the latest tests show that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games have never performed better on Mac…

Apple has a dedicated game porting toolkit, specifically designed to help developers assess how their Windows games will perform on Mac. The idea behind it is to encourage and facilitate developers in porting games to the Mac platform.

However, as Filipe Esposito of Macworld pointed out, this toolkit is also being used by gamers to run Windows software unofficially on Mac – he himself is one of them. He says the latest test version has brought about a leap in performance, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

I spent several days testing the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and found that the performance boost fundamentally changes the experience of running demanding Windows games… Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, with identical game settings and benchmarks, the frame rate of GTA V jumped from around 106 fps under GPTK 3 to roughly 176 fps under the GPTK 4 beta — an improvement of about 66%. The game ran at 2K resolution smoothly on medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledges that not every game sees such a dramatic improvement, but hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider Mac a viable platform.
